name: Channelside Fabrication & Machine, LLC
summary: Structural and pipe fabrication, CNC machining and field services for plants, terminals and contractors along the Houston Ship Channel.

emergency.title: Turnaround and breakdown line
emergency.text: Field crews answer around the clock during turnarounds and unplanned outages. Call the main line and press 2.

groups.title: Fabrication
groups.summary: Structural steel, pressure piping and skid packages cut, fit and welded to your drawings.
groups.intro: From a single pipe rack to a full process skid, fabrication is planned against your drawings and specification, welded by certified welders to qualified procedures, and inspected before it ships.

services.title: Structural Steel
services.text: Pipe racks, platforms, stairs, handrail and support steel for new units and revamps.

services.title: Pressure Piping
services.text: Carbon, stainless and chrome spools fabricated to ASME B31.3.

services.title: Skids and Modules
services.text: Process, metering and chemical injection skids built, piped and tested in the shop.

groups.title: Machining
groups.summary: CNC turning and milling for new parts, reverse engineered parts and repairs.
groups.intro: A machine shop sized for heavy industrial work: large-swing lathes, a horizontal boring mill and five-axis milling, run by machinists who read a worn part as well as a print.

services.title: CNC Turning
services.text: Shafts, sleeves, flanges and threaded connections, one-off or in production runs.

services.title: CNC Milling
services.text: Three, four and five-axis milling for housings, manifolds and fixtures.

services.title: Repair and Reverse Engineering
services.text: Worn and broken parts measured, drawn and made new when the maker no longer supplies them.

groups.title: Field Services
groups.summary: On-site machining, welding and installation during turnarounds and outages.
groups.intro: Crews and portable equipment go to the unit, so a flange face, a heat exchanger or a pump base is put right without pulling the equipment.

services.title: On-site Machining
services.text: Flange facing, line boring and milling in place with portable machines.

services.title: Turnaround Support
services.text: Welding, fitting and rigging crews scheduled into your turnaround plan.

credentials.label: TWIC
credentials.detail: Field crews cleared for port and terminal work

steps.title: Send the drawings
steps.text: Drawings, a specification or the worn part itself, with the date it is needed.

steps.title: Get a written quote
steps.text: Price, lead time and the inspection plan, usually within two working days.

steps.title: Build and inspect
steps.text: Fabricated or machined in the shop, then inspected and documented.

steps.title: Deliver to the unit
steps.text: Shipped on our trucks in erection order, or installed by a field crew.

about.title: Thirty years on the ship channel.
text: Channelside started in 1994 as a two-bay welding shop serving the plants along Market Street. It grew with its customers, adding a machine shop, a pipe shop and field crews as the work called for them.
Today the shop runs two shifts on a ten-acre yard in Channelview, a few minutes from the refineries, terminals and chemical plants it works for.
Most of the work comes from customers who have been sending drawings for twenty years or more.

values.title: Safety first, every shift
values.text: Every crew member can stop a job that is not safe.

values.title: Quality you can document
values.text: Material certificates, weld maps and inspection reports with every job.

values.title: Dates that hold
values.text: A lead time is quoted to be kept, not to win the job.

faqs.q: What do you need to quote a job?
faqs.a: Drawings or a sketch with dimensions, the material and the specification, the quantity and the date it is needed. For a repair, the worn part or a photo of it.

faqs.q: Do you work inside plant gates?
faqs.a: Yes. Field crews carry the site safety training and TWIC cards the work calls for, and the company is a member contractor on ISNetworld.
Yes, on our own trucks across the Houston area and to Louisiana, in the order the pieces will be erected.
